observed_behavior: On Linux, two BUG owner contract tests fail because ordinary existing POSIX paths are classified as symlink or reparse redirects, which also suppresses the smallest-revision diagnostic.
expected_behavior: Ordinary POSIX paths are accepted, genuine symlinks remain fail closed, and the smallest available positive assessment revision is enforced.
impact: The defect blocks the approved Linux full-test and release gates for this delivery while Windows verification remains green.

reproduction.symptom_oracle: The Linux owner suite reports exactly two failures before correction; ordinary directories classify false, genuine symlinks true, and all 19 tests pass after the single-variable correction.
steps: Run the BUG owner contract suite in the native Linux validation copy.
Probe _is_reparse_path on an ordinary temporary directory.
Replace only missing POSIX st_file_attributes handling at runtime and rerun the two focused failures.
reproduction.sample: Full suite reproduced in one of one attempts; the two focused cases passed in one of one controlled pre/post attempts.

root_cause.summary: The POSIX stat result has no st_file_attributes member. _is_reparse_path catches that AttributeError together with operating-system errors and returns true, so normal paths are misclassified; treating the absent Windows-only member as zero restores both failed invariants without weakening actual symlink rejection.

next_action: Implementation executor transitions Verifying to Fixing, invalidates WP-003 and downstream WP-004, captures regression red, applies the one-cause POSIX classification fix, and reruns owner plus Windows/Linux full verification before fresh review.
